clue.text: 5 down player and American writer, name of Lee

definitions.meaning: someone who plays music on a harp
the first name of the author of To Kill a Mockingbird

explanation.walkthrough: '5 down' points to MUSIC, so the first definition is a musician; the second is the forename of the novelist Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp player is a musician, and the same word is the given name of the American novelist Lee.

clue.text: Thermodynamic formula, one possibly a bit acid

parts.note: the article a can stand for one, as in 'a dozen' meaning one dozen

indicators.note: a formula is a recipe for mixing things, so the letters of the following words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A chemistry formula is described as possibly slightly acidic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formula' looks like part of the definition but signals the rearranging of A BIT ACID into DIABATIC, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An adiabatic process in physics is one with no heat gained or lost, a central idea of thermodynamics.

clue.text: Girl entertaining family in city, formerly

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Peg is a girl's name, short for Margaret
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: A girl hosts her relatives in some city in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Peking is the older Western spelling of the name of the Chinese capital, now Beijing.

clue.text: Why not let everyone have as much beer as they want?

parts.words: not let everyone have as much
parts.note: to ration a thing is to limit each person's share of it
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A question about why drinkers cannot have all the beer they want.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a complaint about rationing; 'as they want' simply completes the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind something, the answer to the question why.

clue.text: Scotsman's far away river for all in 21 letters

indicators.note: the letters of the cross-referenced word are taken loose and set in a new order around the extra one

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences
the answer to 21 down

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's remote river is defined in terms of letters from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 21 letters' puts U among the letters of MARRY (21 down), rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Murray is Australia's longest river, named after a Scottish statesman, and Murray is also a common Scottish surname.

clue.text: Sound of cat? Yes, that's correct

annotationWithheld.why: Sound of cat? Yes, that's correct (5): MEW + SIC said aloud, but 'Sound' is both the definition and the homophone signal, one word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sound of cat? Yes, that's correct

clue.text: Beans, say, in scarlet are rejected

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
beans are an example of pulses, edible seeds

explanation.surface: Some beans in a red dish are sent back by a diner.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repulsed is to be driven back or turned away, the same as being rejected.

clue.text: Humiliate a singer, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a bass is a male singer with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: A question whether to embarrass a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower them in dignity, to humble or humiliate them.

clue.text: It's sporting an animated conscience

definitions.meaning: a bat-and-ball game played in summer in England
Jiminy, the insect who acts as Pinocchio's conscience in the Disney cartoon

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is England's summer bat-and-ball game; Jiminy Cricket is the conscience in Disney's cartoon Pinocchio.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the English summer sport and the insect who serves as Pinocchio's conscience in the cartoon.

clue.text: "Teacher wrote 5 down" — report is put around

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: a teacher is addressed as sir, and to write music is to compose it

explanation.surface: A report that a teacher composed some music.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR COMPOSED, said aloud, makes the rare word for placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumposed means placed round about something, from Latin circum, around.

clue.text: Start of Strauss opera with no middle and no top part

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken
the central letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describes a Strauss opera stripped of its middle and missing its top part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no middle' drops the E from OPERA, leaving OPRA.
explanation.definitionFit: In part-singing the soprano carries the highest line, the top part of the harmony.

clue.text: Apply too much pressure to passages of 8 across — time to go back to church

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls, a passage of play
RET is an abbreviation for return, as on rail fares

explanation.surface: A warning against pushing too hard during cricket, before it is time to return to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across is CRICKET; RET for return is unusual, seen on travel tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstretch is to strain something beyond its limits, putting it under too much pressure.

clue.text: Cambridge's latest birds find study of cancer largely — two thirds myth

parts.note: robins are small birds

indicators.note: most of the following word is kept, its ending lost

parts.note: oncology is the medical study of tumours

indicators.note: only two thirds of the word's letters are kept, its final third lost

parts.note: a legend is a traditional story

explanation.surface: Birds discover that most of cancer research is largely mythical, in Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: ONCOLOGY loses OGY to give ONCOL; LEGEND keeps four of its six letters, LEGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson College, founded in 1979, is the newest of the University of Cambridge's colleges.

clue.text: I'm very busy so I wear the burka

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being overwhelmed with work
a burka covers the body to the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: someone in a burka is covered as far as the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means swamped with work, and literally describes being covered to eye level.

clue.text: Little birds here should be feature of wedding — Euan Blair's?

parts.note: a hat is a typical feature of a wedding outfit
Cherie Blair is Euan Blair's mother, so the hat at his wedding would be Cherie's

explanation.surface: A remark on the headgear at the wedding of Tony Blair's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Euan is the son of former Prime Minister Tony Blair and Cherie Blair; HAT CHERIE'S joins up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatcheries are places where eggs are hatched, so young birds are found there.

clue.text: Curmudgeon embracing offspring nearly 19 years older than 11

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a churl is a surly, ill-bred person

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: a child is offspring

explanation.surface: A grumpy man hugs a child, apparently nineteen years his senior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims CHILD to CHIL. 11 is ROBINSON COLLEGE (1979); Churchill College dates from 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill College, Cambridge, was founded in 1960, nineteen years before Robinson College.

clue.text: Zenith possible for one mentally ready to achieve it

indicators.note: possible means one of several arrangements, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reaching the zenith is possible for someone mentally ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges ZENITH into INTHEZ; ONE follows it unchanged, joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the zone is an idiom for a state of complete focus in which one performs at one's best.

clue.text: Permit astronomer to drop drug with fatal effect

parts.note: to let is to permit

indicators.note: dropping a letter means removing it from the word

parts.note: Edmond Halley, the astronomer after whom the comet is named
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Allowing an astronomer to give up drugs has deadly results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' takes E out of HALLEY, leaving HALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethally means in a deadly way, with fatal effect.

clue.text: Fairy before returning sweet is ready to be kissed

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous fairy in A Midsummer Night's Dream
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A fairy anticipates a returning dessert while waiting for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns PUD into DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lips puckered up are pursed in readiness for a kiss.

clue.text: Mark beginning, not ending

indicators.note: without its last letter, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: A line about marking a beginning but not an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ending' removes the final T of START.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a mark such as an asterisk, used to highlight something.

clue.text: Public servants at one in 5 down

definitions.meaning: The large British trade union for public service workers
in music, voices singing the same note together

explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is MUSIC; the British union for public service workers has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the British public service workers' union and music sung at one pitch.

clue.text: A lot of 5 down, or my Scotch penny is counterfeit

indicators.note: a counterfeit coin is a false one, so these letters are made up into something new

explanation.surface: A remark that a Scottish penny is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is MUSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony concert presents a large programme of orchestral music, a lot of it in one evening.

clue.text: Scottish queen — imprisoned queen indeed!

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Mary, Queen of Scots
R is short for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The Scottish queen was indeed imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish queen Mary really was imprisoned, by Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Marry is an archaic exclamation of surprise or emphasis, meaning indeed.

clue.text: Couldn't Alfred make up his mind?

definitions.text: Couldn't Alfred make up his mind?

parts.words: Couldn't Alfred make up his mind?
parts.note: the poet Alfred's surname splits into a refusal followed by an agreement

explanation.walkthrough: Alfred is the English poet of The Highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Alfred, author of The Highwayman, has a surname that reads as a word of refusal then one of assent.

clue.text: Repair to meadow with the man who contrived to 21 its clue

definitions.text: the man who contrived to 21 its clue

parts.note: to darn is to mend a hole in fabric
a ley is grassland or pasture

explanation.surface: Fixing things in a meadow with the fellow who managed to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down's clue is 'Scottish queen'; Lord Darnley married Mary, Queen of Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Darnley managed to marry Mary, Queen of Scots, the subject of 21 down's clue.

clue.text: 21 inversely bein' emollient

indicators.note: inversely means turned about, so the end of the word swaps round to the front

parts.note: soothing, with its final g dropped as in casual speech

explanation.surface: An archaic exclamation from someone being soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inversely' moves IN from the end of SOOTHIN' to the front. 21 is MARRY, an old word meaning indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: In sooth is an archaic phrase meaning in truth, the same sense as the exclamation marry.

clue.text: See 12
One desiring to be extended?

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is one who longs; the second is the comparative of long.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who yearns and the comparative of long, meaning more extended.
